title: Auric Edge - Quickstart options & TTFT (hosted vs dedicated)
summary: Initial discovery focused on time-to-first-token (TTFT) for ML prototype, tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated, data residency and KMS requirements, and next steps to provision credits and run a short benchmark. Customer leaned toward trying hosted quickstart but wanted SOC2 + KMS info before sending PII-adjacent sample data.
next_steps: Redwood to provision 50k free credit bundle and send onboarding link
Redwood SE to share SOC 2 summary, network diagram, and KMS/HSM integration notes
Schedule 1-hour bench session w/ Auric Eng to run latency/cost perf (target next week)
Customer to confirm timeline and dataset subset for bench (safe, non-PII sample)
Follow-up call: demo of Console observability and rollout policies
action_items: Sophie Martinez: provision free credits and send quickstart guide (due: 2026-11-27)
Daniel Cho: prepare benchmark runbook and example scripts for Docker/VPC access (due: 2026-11-30)
Maya Patel: share sample sanitized dataset and target QPS/latency SLOs (due: 2026-12-01)
Riya Shah: compile list of compliance questions re: KMS and data deletion (due: 2026-11-29)
transcript:
00:00:03 Sophie: hey everybody, thanks for joining. this is Sophie from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. Daniel who's our solutions engineer is here as well. really quick — can we do quick intros?
00:00:12 Maya: hi, i'm Maya, CTO at Auric Edge. we run the personalization stack, mostly customer-facing recommendations.
00:00:18 Liam: liam, eng manager, i'll own the integration work.
00:00:21 Riya: riy a, secops, i'll be on the security side.
00:00:25 Daniel: great to meet you all. quick agenda: TTFT, hosting options, security, and then a proposed pilot.
00:00:35 Sophie: perfect. to start, can you give us context — what is your timeline and how fast do you need to get to first request?
00:00:42 Maya: we have a hard internal milestone for an alpha in six weeks, but ttft we want as fast as possible — devs expect to spike an MVP in days not weeks.
00:00:51 Liam: specifically, we want to wire a chat endpoint to our product and see sub-200ms latencies for the UI flows in staging.
00:00:58 Sophie: ok, that helps. typically teams do a hosted quickstart to get to first token — we can get you keys and a small credits bundle, usually devs hit first token in under an hour if they follow the quickstart.
00:01:10 Maya: under an hour? sounds good. what's the catch — like rate limits or throttling?
00:01:15 Daniel: on hosted we have default rate limits but they're conservative; we can bump them during the credit pilot. important callouts: our hosted API includes streaming, embeddings, and reranking. also we have model variants; if you need lower cost at the expense of latency we can route to quantized variants.
00:01:33 Riya: question on data: our product ingests customer PII. can you explain how data is handled on hosted? encryption at rest, kms, etc.
00:01:41 Sophie: yes — we do encryption at rest, SOC2 controls, and we support customer-managed keys in our Private offering. for hosted we offer provider-managed KMS but we also have guidance for bring-your-own-key in Dedicated or Private.
00:01:56 Maya: hmm we might be able to sanitize the sample but later we'll need KMS. what about audit logs?
00:02:03 Daniel: Console provides per-request tracing and token-level cost breakdown. audit logs are available as a retention add-on. we can share an example network diagram.
00:02:14 Liam: thanks. technical question: what's the runtime stack look like — do we have to run an agent or any SDK?
00:02:20 Daniel: no agents for hosted. SDKs are client-side only. for Dedicated you run in a reserved pool under our orchestration, and for Private we ship a control plane to your VPC. general flow is identical — same API surface.
00:02:33 Sophie: another common decision point is cost vs latency. Dedicated gives you capacity isolation which helps tail latency, hosted gives best time-to-first-token.
00:02:43 Maya: can you quantify cost differences? we have a tight unit-economics model.
00:02:47 Daniel: roughly — hosted per-token pricing is variable, Dedicated is on a reserved commit plus lower per-token; Optimize suggests batching settings so you can tune. exact numbers depend on model class and qps. we can provide a cost run sheet after we see your expected sequence lengths.
00:03:05 Riya: also we'd need SSO integration for Console — SAML or OIDC?
00:03:09 Sophie: both. we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning.
00:03:13 Maya: ok good. back to TTFT: for the quickstart, what do devs actually do?
00:03:18 Daniel: step 1: create account and claim credits, step 2: grab API key from console, step 3: run example curl or our python SDK — the example app demonstrates streaming and caching with an in-memory KV cache for prefix caching. most teams see first token in a few minutes on a laptop.
00:03:36 Liam: you said KV cache — you mean KV like key-value cache?
00:03:39 Daniel: yes, sorry it's the prefix/KV cache — sometimes the transcription turns it into K V cash haha.
00:03:46 Maya: (laughter) fair. for our alpha we want to prototype on hosted, but we may need Dedicated later for latency and data controls. how hard is it to move from hosted to Dedicated?
00:03:56 Sophie: we try to make it seamless. same API and model versions. migration is mostly around provisioning capacity, updating routing policies, and, if you need CMK, configuring keys. Daniel can run the migration checklist.
00:04:08 Daniel: yes, and we support canary rollouts and model pins so you can test traffic split before full migration.
00:04:15 Riya: audit and compliance — does hosted delete request logs on demand? we need data retention controls.
00:04:22 Sophie: there are retention policies and a deletion API. for stricter SLAs we recommend Dedicated or Private.
00:04:28 Maya: ok. can we run a short latency/cost benchmark with a sanitized payload? we want to measure p95 and cost per 1k tokens.
00:04:35 Daniel: absolutely. we normally run a small bench: canned prompts, sequence length distribution, and target QPS. we'll run hosted first — it gives you realistic SLOs — then if you need, repeat on Dedicated.
00:04:46 Liam: timeline — you said you can provision credits quickly?
00:04:50 Sophie: yes, i'll provision a 50k credit pack and send the onboarding link after this call. Daniel will send the bench runbook and sample scripts.
00:04:58 Maya: great. one more thing — vendor risk: do you have a SOC2 report and penetration test summary we can share with security?
00:05:06 Sophie: yes, we'll include SOC2 type II summary and pen test attestation. note that the private/on-prem path has additional controls if that's required.
00:05:15 Riya: and kms in hosted — you said provider-managed only? we really prefer CMK for production.
00:05:20 Sophie: CMK is supported in Dedicated via integrations with common cloud KMS and in Private we support HSM/KMS solutions. we'll include KMS integration notes.
00:05:30 Maya: ok that answers most of it. what's success criteria for the pilot from your perspective?
00:05:36 Daniel: measurable: get to first token (<1 hour), run bench with p95 < target (you set target), and review cost per 1k tokens. also run a demo of Console to validate tracing and alerts.
00:05:48 Liam: our p95 target is 200-250ms for the interactive path in staging.
00:05:53 Maya: we'll aim to have sanitized dataset and acceptance criteria by next Wednesday.
00:05:58 Sophie: perfect. i'll recap in the follow-up email with links and the onboarding. any other questions?
00:06:03 Maya: not right now. thanks everyone.
00:06:06 Riya: thanks.
00:06:07 Daniel: thanks all, we'll send materials.
00:06:10 Sophie: bye everyone.
questions: How long to move from hosted quickstart to Dedicated?
What observability is provided per-request (token-level breakdown)?
Is there an on-demand deletion API for logs and request traces?
